picks.setup: Director buys after a 9.3% post-earnings drop
picks.stageN: Fell 9.3% after the Oct 29 report; no current price in the source.
picks.why: Director James Fish Jr. bought 1,000 shares on Nov 2 at about $620.39 ($620,390), filed Nov 3. Q3 sales rose 17% to $20.7B vs $20.8B expected; adjusted EPS was $7.20 vs $4.95 and operating margin 20.4% vs 17.3%.
picks.risk: Revenue slightly missed and the stock fell 9.3% on the report. One purchase is small against the share price, and the source gives no price or valuation data.

picks.setup: Director buy with volume above average
picks.stageN: Below its 50-day ($52.80) and 200-day ($58.36) averages, near the 52-week low.
picks.why: Director Matthew Cohn bought 1,000 shares on Nov 3 at $45.54 ($45,540), raising his stake 1.61% to 63,111. Volume was 850,319 vs a 521,486 average; P/E is 8.35 and the average analyst target is $63.88.
picks.risk: Q3 revenue was $135.89M vs $154.86M expected, a large miss, and the trend is still down. The purchase is small.

picks.setup: CEO buy, stock about 33% under its high
picks.why: CEO Suresh Krishna bought 750 shares on Nov 2 at $69.52 ($52,140), raising his stake 2.49% to 30,897. Q3 EPS was $0.63 vs $0.60 expected and revenue $154.32M (+13.7%) vs $149.31M; average target is $100.50.
picks.risk: P/E is 46.6, Weiss cut it to hold (c+) on Nov 3, and the stock trades under both averages. The buy is small (about $52K).

picks.setup: Three insiders buying in the same week
picks.stageN: Lead only: no price, volume or valuation data was verified.
picks.why: Quiver's Nov 3 list shows CEO Jeffrey Hirsch bought 5,000 shares for $110,650 on Nov 2 (three purchases, 25,000 shares, $565,850 in total). Scott MacDonald bought 5,000 shares ($102,950) and James Kapenstein 1,460 shares ($36,236).
picks.risk: Only the filings are verified; there is no price, trend or fundamentals data here, so treat it as a lead to research.

picks.setup: Call volume about 82% above normal
picks.stageN: Rose 5.9% to $12.40 but still far under its 200-day average ($17.21).
picks.why: 48,052 calls traded vs a typical 26,427 (about 82% above). The shares rose 5.9% to $12.40 on Nov 4, against a 52-week range of $10.03 to $27.61.
picks.risk: Option flow alone says little about direction, and the stock sits about 28% under its 200-day average. No Nov 5 update was found.

picks.setup: Directors buy a beaten-down stock
picks.stageN: Closed Nov 5 at $172.50, near the bottom of its 52-week range.
picks.why: Directors Buckley (5,820 shares, about $998K) and Mollenkopf (2,950 shares, about $510K) bought on Oct 30. Backlog is $745B and free cash flow guidance steps from $2B in 2026 to $10B in 2029.
picks.risk: On the author's math the stock is 68x 2026 free cash flow, and Q3 adjusted EPS missed (-$0.34 vs -$0.25). The buys are small against the share price.
picks.srcN: Motley Fool, Nov 3; Quiver Quant, Nov 4

picks.setup: CEO bought near $64.73; stock now well below
picks.stageN: Closed Nov 5 at $52.25 (-10.33%), about 19% below the CEO buy price.
picks.why: CEO Lip-Bu Tan bought 150,000 shares on Nov 2 at about $64.73 (about $9.7M). Intel fell 28.6% on Oct 30 on a weaker Q4 outlook, then 10.33% more on Nov 5 in the chip selloff.
picks.risk: The CEO buy is already well underwater and the chip group is in a sharp selloff. Management expects PC weakness into 1H 2027.
picks.srcN: Quiver Quant, Nov 4; Stock Titan, Nov 5

picks.setup: Beat and raise on a day the Nasdaq fell 5.5%
picks.why: EPS was $0.38 vs $0.34 expected and revenue $782.5M vs $736.8M. The company raised its full-year outlook. Shares were up about 17% after hours.
picks.risk: After-hours moves can fade at the open, and the market just had its worst day since April 2025. Price and volume were not in the source.

picks.cat: Q3 beat, Q4 guide above Street (Nov 5)
picks.setup: Beat, higher revenue guide, premarket pop
picks.why: EPS was $3.16 vs $2.85 expected and revenue $4.87B vs $4.75B. The Q4 revenue guide was above estimates and 2026 revenue growth guidance was raised. Shares were up about 12.1% premarket Nov 6.
picks.risk: Premarket gains can reverse at the open, and the jobs report at 8:30 ET can move everything. No volume data in the source.
picks.srcN: Yahoo Finance (Motley Fool), Nov 6; CappNotes, Nov 5

picks.cat: Fiscal Q1 report, cautious cloud outlook (Nov 5)

picks.why: Atlassian beat estimates but guided cautiously for cloud subscriptions. Shares were down about 16% after hours and 15.6% premarket on Nov 6.
picks.risk: Gap-downs can extend or bounce, and software names are swinging with the AI selloff. The source gives no price or volume.
picks.srcN: Yahoo Finance (Motley Fool), Nov 6; CappNotes, Nov 5

picks.setup: Miss and a lower full-year revenue guide
picks.why: DraftKings missed estimates and cut its full-year revenue guidance. Shares were down about 18% after hours.
picks.risk: The source gives only the move, with no price, volume or detail on the miss. After-hours quotes differ from the open.

picks.setup: Earnings after a 12% drop
picks.why: Closed Nov 5 at $45.99 (-12.18%), about 70% under its record close of $150.23. Consensus is about -$0.02 EPS on $256.51M revenue; Q3 gross margin is guided to 35-37%.
picks.risk: The Neutron rocket slipped to 2027 and the stock trades near 30x sales. Earnings can gap it either way.

picks.why: Fell 16.36% on Nov 5 in the chip selloff. The board approved a $25B buyback and the shares firmed after hours.
picks.risk: The buyback has no stated timetable and the whole chip group is moving together. No price or valuation data in the source.

picks.setup: Sharp pullback in a strong theme
picks.why: Fell 17.46% to $656.39 on Nov 5, about 48% under its 52-week high. Chip stocks bounced 5% to 8.3% premarket Nov 6 (Yahoo).
picks.risk: Memory is cyclical, the Nov 6 bounce may not hold, and policy fears around data centers are unresolved.

picks.setup: Q3 beat and a guidance raise
picks.why: Q3 revenue rose 38.6% to $24.40B vs $22.62B expected. Mounjaro sales were $10.72B (+65%) and Zepbound $5.35B (+49%). Gross margin is 83.6%; forward P/E is 30x vs Novo 12x.

picks.setup: Dominant robot platform after a guidance drop
picks.why: Q3 revenue rose 22% to $3.05B and da Vinci procedures rose 14%. Gross margin is 67.2%, and by some estimates fewer than 8% of eligible soft-tissue procedures are done robotically.
picks.risk: Weaker procedure guidance drove the post-earnings drop; da Vinci 5 margin pressure and competition from Medtronic and J&J are cited. The source gives no analyst targets.

picks.setup: Rebound candidate with a 2.9% yield
picks.why: Forward P/E is 16 with a 2.90% dividend yield. Q2 comparable sales rose 3.8% and EPS was $4.11 vs $2.05 a year earlier.
picks.risk: Sales and profits fell in recent years, gross margin is only 26.8%, and the source cites no analyst targets.

picks.setup: Fast grower near its 52-week low

picks.risk: Profits have fallen as it spends on growth. The article does not explain the Nov 5 drop, which coincided with the broad tech selloff.

picks.setup: Growth brand down 27% this year

picks.risk: Competition from Nike and Lululemon. The source gives no analyst targets.

picks.setup: Post-earnings drop after a run-up
picks.stageN: Ran 13.8% into earnings on Nov 4, then fell 9.6% on Nov 5.
picks.why: Q3 revenue was $1,022M (+12%) with a net loss of $0.23 per share vs $0.12 a year ago. The Q4 guide calls for at least 40% revenue growth and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $70M-$85M. Alpha Vantage shows a $1.79 close on 43.1M shares.
picks.risk: The per-share loss widened from a year ago, cash and share count were not checked, and mortgage rates are still above 7%.
picks.srcN: Opendoor 8-K exhibit, Nov 5; Alpha Vantage, Nov 5

picks.cat: FDA ANDA approved Oct 30; Nov 10 goal date moot
picks.setup: Approval announced before the goal date
picks.stageN: Rose 11.2% on Nov 4, then fell 8.8% on Nov 5 with the catalyst already resolved.
picks.why: An 8-K says the FDA approved the preservative-free ketamine ANDA on Oct 30, ahead of the Nov 10 GDUFA goal date. Alpha Vantage shows a $2.27 close on 832,743 shares.
picks.risk: The dated catalyst is gone, so the stock now trades on follow-through. Cash and share count were not checked.

picks.setup: Spike on a routine filing, now fading
picks.stageN: Spiked 55.5% on Nov 4, then gave back 23.4% on Nov 5 on 11.9M shares.
picks.why: Curis jumped as much as 142% premarket on Nov 4 after a routine proxy filing, closed at $1.11, then fell to $0.85 on Nov 5 (volume 11.9M).
picks.risk: Cash was about $5.6M against a quarterly loss near $8.6M, so it will probably need to raise money. A study example of a trap.

picks.cat: Nasdaq suspension at Nov 5 open unless a hearing was requested
picks.setup: Delisting determination after three reverse splits
picks.stageN: Closed Nov 5 at $0.164 (-48.6%) on 26.3M shares, after -88.3% on Nov 4.
picks.why: Nasdaq issued a delisting determination on Oct 27 after 30 straight days under $1. Three reverse splits (a cumulative 1-for-2,000) leave no compliance period, and authorized shares rose from 350M to 850M on Oct 30.
picks.risk: Whether the company filed for a hearing is unconfirmed, so suspension remains possible. A study example of a trap.
